subject: chopperMotorbike
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: custom chopper motorbike.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a chopper motorcycle build using the available geometry API, working out proportions like overall length, wheel size, and orientation before constructing the module.

For the design, I'm going with an Overwatch-style look: fat rear tire, raked front fork, teardrop tank, springer seat, ape-hanger bars, and a glowing V-twin engine with bold orange/graphite/white color blocking and cyan accent strips.

Now I'm calculating the frame geometry -- placing axle positions, working out the fork rake angle from the head tube to the front axle, and setting up the joint hierarchy (frame, fork, wheelF, wheelR) before building out the tires and connecting tubes.

Shaping tire profiles for the lathe geometry...

Still building out the bike parts...

Still working out cylinder tilt angles...

Now I'm mapping out the exhaust pipe geometry—a tapering drag pipe sweeping from the front cylinder port back along the side with chrome shading, mirrored on both sides, plus sketching the hardtail frame rods running from the head tube down through the backbone.

Then I shift to the rear swingarm rails and seat stays flanking the wheel, and work out the seat as a flattened sphere shape for a leather look, with a rod standing in for coil springs underneath and a curved sweep planned for the rear fender arch.

Now I'm sketching the headlamp as a glowing cyan-white sphere lens up front and a small red glow for the taillight.

Next I'm adding cyan glow strips under the tank frame, then placing an Overwatch emblem decal as a small plane texture curved against the tank sides near the frame body. I'm also setting up the ground positioning so the tires sit flush at y=0, computing tire radii so the rear and front wheel centers rest correctly on the ground plane.

Now I'm writing the wheel-building function that generates hubs, spoke rings made from rotated boxes, and lathe-based tires, along with the frame color palette including graphite, orange, chrome, and cyan paints.

I'm setting up the joints hierarchy: steering joint connecting steer to frame near the head, wheel joints for front and rear axles, and the root frame joint. Then I'm adding fork rods, a triple clamp box at the head, and positioning a forward-facing headlight sphere scaled flatter in the z-axis.

Now adding the lens as a flat circle, then sweeping arcs for the front and rear fenders using angle ranges around the wheel axles with slightly different radii for front versus rear coverage, plus handlebars attached to the steer bone before finishing up the export, making sure to keep the mirrored geometry loops consistent.
